root.name: Ponziani Opening: Jaenisch Counterattack
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. c3 Nf6

overview: Black meets 3.c3 with a counterattack on e4 instead of allowing d4. After 4.d4 Nxe4 5.d5 Ne7 6.Nxe5 White wins the e5 pawn back and gets a space edge, but Black has active pieces and ...Ng6 and ...d6 ideas; 4.d4 exd4 5.e5 is also played. 4.d3 is a quiet alternative. The game is open and tactical in the main lines.

white_ideas.idea: 4.d4 Nxe4 5.d5 Ne7 6.Nxe5 for a space edge and active pieces
Pawn exchanges and open lines to use the lead in development
4.d3 for a quieter game, a slow build-up

black_ideas.idea: Counterattack on e4 and develop quickly
Trade pieces and play for ...d5 break

typical_structures.structure: Open Game centre where White pawns advance with d5 and Black develops freely

character.notes: The main 4.d4 Nxe4 5.d5 line is open and tactical, with pieces hanging; the 4.d3 branch is quiet.

gambit.notes: Pawns are exchanged; no clear gambit.

soundness.notes: Sound; White keeps a small edge.

structure.notes: Open lines in the main line, pawn centre exchanged.

approach.notes: Standard but uncommon; the Ponziani is a surprise weapon more than a main-line choice.

level.notes: Some lines to know but nothing deep.

sublines_that_differ.name: 4.d3
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. c3 Nf6 4. d3
sublines_that_differ.how: Quiet, plays like a reversed Philidor structure.

character.reason: Main line 4.d4 Nxe4 5.d5 is forcing and tactical.

approach.reason: Less common, but strong players do choose it from time to time.
